statements.text: Base $AB=12$ cm and perpendicular height $CH=4$ cm give area $\frac{1}{2}\times 12\times 4=24$ cm$^{2}$.
A slanted side from $C$ that is not perpendicular to the line through $AB$ can replace $CH$ as the height.
The same base–perpendicular-height product gives the area for every type of triangle.

stem: Javed has triangle $ABC$ with $AB=12$ cm. From $C$ he draws a perpendicular to the line through $AB$, meeting it at $H$, and measures $CH=4$ cm.

teacher.key_rationale: Area is ½×base×perpendicular height, so statements 1 and 3 are true. Statement 2 drops the perpendicular condition. Including 2 with 1, or only 2 with 3, or all three, is wrong.
